accuracy.evidence: Matches CCSS L.5.3a (expand, combine and reduce sentences for meaning, reader interest and style) and NC 2013 Years 5-6 writing (relative clauses, commas to clarify meaning, grammar chosen for effect). Grammar checked against the KS2 glossary and Purdue OWL: and/so are co-ordinating (equal clauses), when/because subordinating; 'a scruffy terrier' is an appositive needing paired commas; 'Suddenly,' is a fronted adverbial; 'returned back', '6 pm in the evening', 'small little' and 'really very' are redundancies (Purdue OWL Conciseness). Only 'final' is offered as the cut in 'final end' because cutting 'end' would change the noun. Numeric items a-b, a+b and a stay positive at every corner.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets documented upper-primary writing errors: longer means better / rambling 'and' chains (aim scene, robot claim 1, m4, challenge tag 'long'), 'and' shows cause (combine predict, robot claim 3, p1, challenge 'and'), the missing second comma around an appositive or relative clause (expand predict, robot claim 5, p2, m6, challenge 'comma'), and cutting words that carry meaning (trim feedback 'carries meaning', twin-cut feedback, m3, challenge 'meaning').

lab_distinct.evidence: flagsenvar works on the three sentence operations themselves: a join scene that requires an equal-clause join then a dependent-clause join of the same pair, a word-tile sentence with dashed gaps that only accept the add-on that fits (opener, appositive after the noun, place phrase after the verb), and tap-to-strike tiles where each redundancy group needs exactly one cut. It differs from flagsemi (clause boundary punctuation) and the noun-phrase lab; the lab_distinct gate measures it under 30% against every flagship lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner discovers the rules by acting: the same two ideas appear as 'so' and 'When' versions side by side, the appositive gap refuses other add-ons with the reason, the sentence visibly grows to 'Suddenly, the dog, a scruffy terrier, barked at the gate.', and struck-through tiles show the shorter sentence keeps its meaning. The done messages confirm each rule only after the task.

predictions.evidence: Three predictions with tempting wrong options the lab disproves: 'and' as the cause word (only because/When build the dependent version), 'One, before it' for the appositive (the placed chip carries a comma on each side and the robot later flags the one-comma version), and 'Yes, more words, more meaning' (cutting four repeated words leaves the same meaning).

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six challenge questions with every wrong option tagged: and ('"and" only adds ideas...'), short ('Two short sentences leave the reader to guess the link'), comma ('Extra information in the middle of a sentence needs a comma on both sides'), meaning ('That word carries meaning...') and long ('After long sentences, a short one stands out'). In the lab, wrong joins, wrong gaps, meaning-word cuts and twin cuts each get their own message.

readability.evidence: Kid paragraphs are short, one operation each (combine, expand, reduce) with a worked example; the adult text was rewritten into shorter sentences after a first validate run read FK 10.5, and now passes the 9.5 limit. Lab banners are short ('Drag each add-on to its gap', 'Cut the repeats: 2 to go').

no_filler.evidence: Every sentence names an operation, gives an example or a warning. Adult paragraphs give curriculum placement and key words, how each operation helps a reader, the named mistakes, and what each lab scene does. The content gate finds no filler phrases.

mobile.evidence: Checked 360 px screenshots in light and dark: word tiles wrap onto new rows with 13 px bold text and 44 px height, dashed gaps are 44 px wide, add-on chips sit below the sentence, struck-through tiles stay legible on grey, the built sentences fill full-width cards, and aim versions wrap inside 70 px cards. Labelled buttons sit under every scene.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a labelled button twin: Join with and/so/When/because; Put '<add-on>' at the start / after 'the dog' / after 'barked'; Cut '<word>' for every tile; Version 1-3 with the full text in the label; Right and Slip. The canvas aria-label updates with every message, the challenge feedback is a polite live region, and walk.cjs ran axe clean in both themes on desktop and iPhone 13.
